intro: Xenia's housing story is unique in the Miami Valley: the devastating 1974 tornado destroyed nearly half the city, and the 1970s rebuilds that replaced it are now hitting 50 years old — aging roofs and siding at exactly the age when moisture intrusion, and mold, accelerates. Downtown Xenia and the Little Miami River area mix these rebuilds with older survivors. Fifty-year-old flashing, gutters, and basement waterproofing are all aging out together, and river-adjacent humidity doesn't help.
moldNote: Xenia's mold risk is the 1974-rebuild aging curve: a whole generation of 1970s homes hitting 50 at once, with roofs, siding, and basement waterproofing failing in the same decade.
